brief:
Israeli restrictions on food entry are preventing recovery from famine conditions in Gaza, according to an Integrated Food Security Phase Classification report cited by Mondoweiss. Acute malnutrition cases are climbing across the Strip as shipments remain constrained. The impediments to humanitarian aid have left vulnerable populations, particularly young children, facing severe nutritional deficits.

Two-year-old Hashem Abu Mustafa, born in a Rafah tent during the hunger crisis, represents the toll on Gaza's youngest residents. Living conditions in the enclave have deteriorated as food access tightens, leaving families unable to meet basic dietary needs. Aid organizations warn that without increased humanitarian corridors and expanded food deliveries, malnutrition will continue its upward trajectory across the territory.
dek: Israeli restrictions on food entry are stalling recovery from famine in Gaza as malnutrition cases climb, an IPC report finds. Two-year-old Hashem Abu Mustafa, born hungry in a Rafah tent, may already be beyond saving.
title: Israeli food restrictions block Gaza famine recovery as malnutrition surges
